loudness.quote: Doesn't move at all. Probably something with remappings and/or cmd_vel_mux

resolution.quote: Issue #235: remap fixed but keyop still fails when commanding after auto-docking

notes: Independently re-decided and agree; the eligibility hinge is E2 step 3 and the spec resolves it correctly. E1: issue #235 (corot, 2013-02-25) reports the concrete failure (quote above); the reporter committed the fix the same hour and the maintainer thread closes it. E2: the minimal resolving edit is a launch remap, which would normally be ineligible deployment_wiring, but the parenthetical rule applies -- the provider renamed its output element and the consumer's deployment had to follow: verified in yujin_ocs commit 2c10cf98 (the advertise line changed from "mux_cmd_vel" to "output", quoted above; the same patch makes the name a yaml-configurable 'publisher' key defaulting to output-style names), and in kobuki commit 35682ec3 ('-    <remap from="cmd_vel_mux/mux_cmd_vel" to="mobile_base/commands/velocity"/>' '+    <remap from="cmd_vel_mux/output" to="mobile_base/commands/velocity"/>'). A provider renaming an element the consumer must follow is an interface change even when the consumer's fix is in a launch file, so the tree does not stop at step 3; steps 4-5 do not apply; step 6 eligible, interface kind topic. Condition class element_removed_or_renamed agree with the provider-side evidence quoted; implicated element topic:cmd_vel_mux/output agree -- one naming caveat recorded: the S1 inventory says 'as the consumer uses them' and the broken consumer referenced the old name cmd_vel_mux/mux_cmd_vel, while the spec records the provider's current name; either string identifies the same element, so this is a form choice, not a disagreement. E3 UPGRADE agree: the consumer launch (authored 2012-12-14 per the spec's notes) still references the output topic 'as they existed at an earlier provider revision', which is exactly the S1 UPGRADE definition; PAIR underlies the data flow and UPGRADE is how the failure was observed. E4 agree ('Doesn't move at all.'). Loudness silent_documented / detection_stage run agree: no diagnostic is shown and none exists for a ROS 1 remap whose source name is never advertised -- the mux simply publishes unremapped while the base waits on mobile_base/commands/velocity. Resolution recommended agree: the commit message itself states the remap is fixed but the residual symptom remains, and the closing comment ('There'is no problem. kobuki_auto_docking used to disable the motors after succeeding.', corot 2013-05-22, read in the comment thread) attributes that residual to motor power, not to showing the corrected composition driving the robot.
